repeat.scenario: You are training as a student assistant at the university library. Listen to the librarian and repeat what she says.
lines: Welcome to the main library.
Please scan your student card at the front gate.
Books on the second floor can be borrowed for two weeks.
If you need help finding a book, ask anyone at the information desk.
Group study rooms must be reserved online at least one day in advance.
Remember to keep your phone on silent and avoid eating near the computers.
Students who return books after the due date will have to pay a small fine before borrowing again.

repeat.scenario: You are learning to welcome visitors to a city zoo. Listen to your manager and repeat what she says.
lines: Thanks for joining today's tour.
The gift shop is next to the main entrance.
Please don't feed the animals, even if they look hungry.
The penguin show starts at eleven, so try to arrive a few minutes early.
Our elephants were rescued from a reserve that closed down last year.
If you get separated from your group, wait by the large fountain near the cafe.
Visitors who buy an annual pass can enter for free on weekends and receive discounts on special events.

repeat.scenario: You are a new student in a chemistry course. Listen to the lab instructor and repeat what he says.
lines: This is the chemistry lab.
Safety glasses must be worn at all times.
The sinks on the left are only for washing equipment.
Write down every measurement in your notebook before you leave.
If anything spills, tell the teaching assistant immediately instead of cleaning it yourself.
Chemicals that are no longer needed go into the labeled containers by the back door.
Anyone who misses the safety training will not be allowed to take part in next week's experiments.

repeat.scenario: You are helping new students move into a residence hall. Listen to the hall director and repeat what she says.
lines: Welcome to Maple Hall.
Your room key is inside this envelope.
Laundry machines are in the basement and accept card payments.
Quiet hours begin at ten on weeknights and at midnight on weekends.
If something in your room is broken, submit a repair request through the housing website.
Each floor has a resident assistant who can help with roommate problems or homesickness.
Residents planning to stay during the winter break must sign up at the front desk by the end of November.

interview.intro: Thank you for taking part in our research study on how people use technology to learn. I'm going to ask you a few questions.
qs: How do you usually learn something new, like a skill or a school subject?
Tell me about an app or a website that helped you learn something.
Some people say online courses are just as effective as classroom courses. Do you agree? Why or why not?
Should universities require every student to take at least one course completely online? Explain your view.

interview.intro: Thanks for joining our study about life in cities. I'd like to ask you some questions about where you live.
qs: Do you live in a big city or a smaller town? What do you like about it?
Describe a public place in your area where people like to spend their free time.
Many cities are replacing parking spaces with parks and bike lanes. Do you think this is a good idea?
Some people believe public transportation should be free for everyone. What is your opinion?

interview.intro: We're researching how young people make decisions about their careers. I have a few questions for you.
qs: What do you do right now for work or study?
Tell me about a person who influenced your choice of career.
Is it better to stay at one company for a long time, or to change jobs every few years? Why?
Some people think companies should let employees work from home permanently. Do you agree or disagree?
